items.informal_name: Coefficient Formula for Hasse Derivative of Order k
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f).coeff n = ↑((n + k).choose k) * f.coeff (n + k)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of a polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ is equal to $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ X^{n + k} $ in $ f $.

items.informal_name: Product Rule for Hasse Derivatives in Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) (f * g) =
    ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.1) f * (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.2) g
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ f, g \in R[X] $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $$ D^{(k)}(f \cdot g) = \sum_{\substack{i + j = k}} D^{(i)}(f) \cdot D^{(j)}(g), $$ where the sum is taken over all pairs $ (i, j) $ of natural numbers such that $ i + j = k $. This expresses the Hasse derivative of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal decomposition of $ k $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Hasse Derivatives and Binomial Coefficients in Laurent Series
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {V : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module R V] (k l : ℕ)
  (f : LaurentSeries V) (n : ℤ),
  ((LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) ((LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R l) f)).coeff n =
    ((k + l).choose k • (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R (k + l)) f).coeff n
items.informal_description: For any natural numbers $k, l$ and Laurent series $f$ with coefficients in an $R$-module $V$, the composition of the $k$-th and $l$-th Hasse derivatives satisfies $\text{hasseDeriv}_k(\text{hasseDeriv}_l f) = \binom{k + l}{k} \cdot \text{hasseDeriv}_{k + l} f$. Specifically, for any integer exponent $n$, the coefficient of $n$ in the composed derivative equals $\binom{k + l}{k}$ multiplied by the coefficient of $n$ in the $(k + l)$-th Hasse derivative of $f$.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient of the Hasse Derivative of Order $ k $ for Laurent Series
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {V : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module R V] (k : ℕ)
  (f : LaurentSeries V) (n : ℤ), ((LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) f).coeff n = Ring.choose (n + ↑k) k • f.coeff (n + ↑k)
items.informal_description: For a fixed natural number $ k $, a Laurent series $ f $ with coefficients in an $ R $-module $ V $, and an integer $ n $, the coefficient of the Hasse derivative $ D^k f $ at exponent $ n $ is given by $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ f $ at exponent $ n + k $. Here, $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ denotes the binomial coefficient defined via the ring's `choose` operation.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative Composition Formula with Binomial Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k l : ℕ),
  Polynomial.hasseDeriv k ∘ₗ Polynomial.hasseDeriv l = (k + l).choose k • Polynomial.hasseDeriv (k + l)
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $ and natural numbers $ k, l $, the composition of the $ k $-th and $ l $-th Hasse derivatives on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ equals $ \binom{k + l}{k} $ times the $ (k + l) $-th Hasse derivative, i.e., $ D^{(k)} \circ D^{(l)} = \binom{k + l}{k} D^{(k + l)} $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Monomial in Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the monomial $ rX^n $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ is given by $ \binom{n}{k} r X^{n - k} $. This expresses how the Hasse derivative acts on monomials by scaling the coefficient by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Hasse Derivatives on Laurent Series
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {V : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module R V] (k l : ℕ)
  (f : LaurentSeries V),
  (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) ((LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R l) f) =
    (k + l).choose k • (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R (k + l)) f
items.informal_description: For any natural numbers $k$ and $l$, and any Laurent series $f$ with coefficients in an $R$-module $V$, the composition of the Hasse derivatives of orders $k$ and $l$ applied to $f$ equals $\binom{k + l}{k} \cdot \text{hasseDeriv}_{k + l}(f)$, where $\text{hasseDeriv}_n(f)$ denotes the Hasse derivative of order $n$.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of a Single Laurent Series Term
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {V : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module R V] (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ)
  (x : V),
  (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) ((HahnSeries.single (n + ↑k)) x) = (HahnSeries.single n) (Ring.choose (n + ↑k) k • x)
items.informal_description: The Hasse derivative of order $k$ applied to the Laurent series with a single non-zero term at exponent $n + k$ and coefficient $x$ results in the Laurent series with a single non-zero term at exponent $n$ and coefficient $\binom{n + k}{k} \cdot x$, where $\binom{n + k}{k}$ denotes the binomial coefficient in the ring $R$.
